# Functional Programming

## Homework Instructions

- Create any dataset you’d like
- Write *two* useful functions:
    - One that creates a plot
    - One that does something else
- Create a Quarto document showing:
    - At least 2 examples per function
    - Evidence of the function’s flexibility
    
## Load libraries
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(PNWColors)
library(sf)
library(maptiles)
library(palmerpenguins)
```
 
## Import data
```{r}
tortoise <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2026/2026-03-03/tortoise_body_condition_cleaned.csv')
```

    
## Conversion Function: Convert fluid ounces to milliliters. 
If we collect a water sample but record it in fluid ounces (Imperial), we would want to easily convert to milliliters (Metric) I've created a function to convert this. 
```{r}
fl_oz_to_ml <- function(fl_oz){
  ml <- (30/1)*(fl_oz)
  return(ml)
}
```
### Example 1 
Confirming that the function works, with the base conversion 1 oz = 30 ml (approximately)
```{r}
fl_oz_to_ml(1)
```
### Example 2
If we input 20 oz into the function, the output is 600ml. 
```{r}
fl_oz_to_ml(20)
```

## Plot Function: Boxplot
Creating the plot function to create boxplots. Add color palette from PNW Colors, remove outliers, and add theme.
```{r}
boxplot <- function(data, x, y, fill, group) {
  pal <- pnw_palette("Sailboat", 3, type = "discrete")
  
  ggplot(data, aes(x = {{x}}, y = {{y}}, fill = {{fill}}, group = {{group}}))+
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA)+
    scale_fill_manual(values = pal)+
    theme_bw()
}
```
### Example 1
Use *palmerpenguins* dataset to plot penguin species and body mass. 
```{r}
#| label: fig-penguin-species-mass
#| fig-cap: "A boxplot showing penguin body mass (g) by penguin species (Adelie, Chinstrap, Gentoo) using palmerpenguins R package."
#| fig-align: "center"
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 10
boxplot(penguins, x = species, y = body_mass_g, fill = species, group = species)+
  labs(x="Species", y="Body Mass (g)", fill = "Species") # add labels
```
### Example 2
Use TidyTuesday dataset *Golem Grad Tortoise Data* to plot tortoise mass and carapace length grouped by locality.
```{r}
#| label: fig-tortoise-flipper-mass
#| fig-cap: "A boxplot showing Hermann's tortoises' straight carapace length (mm) and body mass (g). Colors indicate location (Beach, Konjsko, Plateau) of tortoises recorded in Lake Prespa in North Macedonia."
#| fig-align: "center"
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 10
boxplot(tortoise, x = body_mass_grams, y = straight_carapace_length_mm, fill = locality, group = locality)+
  labs(x="Body Mass (g)", y="Straight Carapace Length (mm)", fill = "Locality") # add labels
```
